sections.heading: Quick review

lines.en: He writes programs.
She's drawing a new design.
Is this your office?

sections.note: Say each phrase aloud before you hear the English.

sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.en: Good morning. What do we do today?
Today is Monday, and we have a meeting.
Where do we sit?
We sit in the big office.
And what do we do in the meeting?

lines.ar: نَتَكَلَّمُ عَنِ الْمَشَارِيعِ، ثُمَّ نَكْتُبُ خُطَّةَ الْأُسْبُوعِ.
lines.en: We talk about the projects, then we write the plan for the week.
Do we drink coffee too?
Of course! We drink coffee and tea together.
And after the meeting?
We work, each one at his own desk.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. It's Monday morning, and a new team member asks Ridhwan about the day.

sections.heading: How it works

lines.en: we write
We work in Lagos.
What do we do today?
Our office is in Lagos.

sections.note: For we, the present tense starts with na: naktubu, we write. You can add nahnu, we, but you don't need it. The ending naa also means our: maktabunaa, our office, and indanaa, we have.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root jeem, meem, ain, meaning gathering

lines.en: he gathered
a university, from faa-il: the one that gathers people
a group, from maf-ool: the things gathered
a meeting, from ifti-aal

sections.note: You know faa-il, the doer, and maf-ool, the thing done to. Today's new pattern is ifti-aal, often an action people do together. Ijtimaa means a meeting: people gathering.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: Do you have a meeting today?
Model answer: Yes, I have a meeting with my team.

lines.ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ مَعَ فَرِيقِكَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
lines.en: What do you do with your team in the morning?
Model answer: We drink tea, then we work together.
Where do you and your team work?
Model answer: We work in our office in Lagos.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
